title: Quadriplegia, paraplegia, monoplegia and spinal cord disorders
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's paralysis or spinal cord condition (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic cauda equina syndrome and bladder management.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old woman presenting for a scheduled evaluation of her chronic cauda equina syndrome. She reports persistent saddle numbness and continues to experience symptoms of bladder retention. She states that she is currently managed with intermittent catheterization and reports that this remains her primary method for maintaining bladder drainage. She denies any new acute neurological deficits or changes in her baseline sensory perception today.

Medication List
1. Oxycodone 5mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
2. Gabapentin 300mg twice daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. She is currently resting in a chair. Physical examination reveals diminished sensation in the saddle region, consistent with her known history of cauda equina syndrome. Motor strength is stable in the lower extremities. Bladder status is managed via catheterization; no signs of systemic infection or urinary tract infection are noted during this visit.

Assessment
1. Chronic cauda equina syndrome with saddle numbness.
2. Chronic bladder retention managed with catheterization.

Plan
Continue current pain management regimen. Continue scheduled catheterization for bladder retention. Follow up in the clinic in three months for a routine neurological and urological assessment.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/14/2026
